_comment: This is a fragment, not a full settings file: merge the "hooks" object below into the user-level ~/.claude/settings.json. It belongs there rather than in a project file because the sessions being watched live in arbitrary repositories, not in this one. Two consequences follow. First, the SessionStart command names its script by a drive-rooted absolute path: a hook runs with the monitored session's own project as its working directory, so a relative path resolves against the wrong repository for every session this project exists to watch, and an environment variable in its place would mean the executed path is attacker-controllable on a machine where anything can set one. That absolute path is specific to this checkout; Section 7's installer substitutes the real one, and wrapper/Enter-ClaudeSession.ps1 refuses to launch when it disagrees with the checkout it is running from. Second, these hooks fire for every session on the machine, including ones started without the wrapper: those carry no CHANNEL_PROCESS_TOKEN, and hooks/session-start.ps1 exits without opening a socket while the broker drops the http hooks' tokenless posts with a 202, because Claude Code surfaces any non-2xx hook response as a visible error inside that session. Every url here must agree with broker/config.ts's DEFAULT_PORT and hooks/session-start.ps1's own literal; settings-fragment.test.ts pins every one of them against those two, because a hook posting into a port nothing is listening on fails silently and makes a working session look unannounced. Five events are declared. SessionStart announces the session and is the only command hook. PostToolUse and the first Stop entry are the liveness ticks feeding the status card, of whose payloads the broker keeps only the session identity, the tool name, and one bounded preview of the tool input, which is why that Stop entry keeps a 2s timeout: a slow broker charges it against the session. PreToolUse is matched to AskUserQuestion alone and is the question alert's emission-time source: Claude Code withholds an open question's transcript line until the picker is answered, so this post is the only signal that exists while the operator could still act on it, and its payload carries the question text, which is why it is the one /hook entry that also carries the mirror switch header. Its timeout is hours long rather than the liveness tick's: the broker's question desk holds this hook's response open while the question is answerable from the session's Discord thread, and the desk's own hold ceiling (broker/config.ts's DEFAULT_QUESTION_HOLD_MS, which is also the CHANNEL_QUESTION_HOLD_MS override's cap) sits a margin below this timeout so a hold always ends in the broker's clean no-decision release, never a client-side timeout error; settings-fragment.test.ts pins that margin. UserPromptSubmit and the second Stop entry are the mirror, carrying the console prompt and the turn's final assistant reply to the Discord thread. The mirror rides its own entries and its own route rather than sharing the liveness ones, so a content-bearing post with a larger body and a longer timeout can never slow or break the tick that keeps a session looking alive. Both mirror hooks are http rather than command scripts for the same reason SessionStart cannot be: a UserPromptSubmit command hook's stdout is injected into the watched session's context exactly as SessionStart's is, so a script there would feed its own output back to the model, while an http hook has no stdout at all and posts its whole payload as the request body, which already carries the prompt text and the turn's last assistant message. The two mirror hooks and the PreToolUse question hook carry a fourth header, X-Channel-Mirror, that the PostToolUse and first-Stop-entry liveness hooks do not, and that SessionStart's command hook has no headers to carry at all: wrapper/Enter-ClaudeSession.ps1's -NoMirror sets CHANNEL_SESSION_MIRROR in the launched session's own environment, and broker/intake.ts reads this header as that one session's escape from the host-wide CHANNEL_MIRROR default in broker.env, a different variable naming a different scope. A session that never set CHANNEL_SESSION_MIRROR sends the header empty, which the broker reads as mirroring on, the same as no header at all; the liveness hooks carry only that bounded tool-input preview, which is deliberately outside this switch: it is a property of the status card, which a no-mirror session still keeps.
_permissions_comment: The relay's reply tool is pre-approved. Without a matching rule the first reply Claude sends opens a permission prompt at the terminal and parks the session until someone answers it at the keyboard, which is the failure this whole project exists to prevent: the operator is on their phone precisely because they are not at that keyboard. The rule name is Claude Code's own for an MCP tool, mcp__<server>__<tool>, built from the name the relay is registered under with every character outside [a-zA-Z0-9_-] replaced by an underscore. One rule ships. Every fleet host runs the plugin route, where the server arrives from plugins/relay and its key is scoped by the plugin carrying it, giving mcp__plugin_relay_channel-relay__reply, the name a live plugin-route session's tool calls carry on the wire. The development route's rule, mcp__channel-relay__reply (built from the wrapper's per-launch --mcp-config registration under $script:ChannelServerName), is deliberately absent: no route in service needs it, and a rule with no route that needs it is a standing squattable pre-approval. A host temporarily back on the development flag parks its first reply on a permission prompt; for a longer stay, add that rule by hand to that host's ~/.claude/settings.json and remove it when the host returns. The names here are held in agreement by install/Install-Functions.ps1's $script:AllowedChannelPermissionRules (the installer merges only names on that list) and the pins in relay/reply-permission.test.ts, install/Install-Functions.test.ts, install/Install-Host.test.ts, and plugins/manifest.test.ts, which holds the plugin-scoped form as a hard literal. docs/install.md carries the per-host checklist.
